newsitem.title: CHILE: Argentina's Maradona falls ill on TV show.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Maradona falls ill on TV show.

text.p: Argentine soccer star Diego Maradona was taken to a clinic on Monday after falling ill while appearing as a guest on a Chilean television programme, officials from the television channel said.

Maradona, who was due to be interviewed during the second part of the talk show, left the stage during an interval after complaining about feeling ill, the hosts of the programme Viva El Lunes on channel Canal 13 said.
Maradona was taken to a nearby clinic for tests and released shortly afterward once doctors determined he was suffering from high blood pressure.
"Maradona suffered high blood pressure as the result of undergoing a very emotional experience," Eduardo Villalon, senior doctor at the clinic, told reporters.

Television stations showed pictures of Maradona, looking pale and anxious, leaving the clinic in a wheelchair to return to his hotel. Doctors said the player, who has undergone treatment for drug addiction, was not suffering from a drug overdose.
Maradona was taken ill shortly after dancing the tango with one of the show's hosts, former Miss Universe Cecilia Bolocco.

Spectators said the player began to look uncomfortable, constantly crossed and uncrossed his arms, and then began to sweat heavily. He asked the host to be allowed to leave but was told to sit until a break in the programme, when he left.
Maradona arrived in Santiago on Monday to take part in the show and to discuss a possible transfer deal to a Chilean football club from Argentine club Boca Juniors.
Chilean media have said Maradona may be in talks with the club Deportes Temuco.
